text:
The AI desktop where every action is visible and approvable before it runs. 

 Rent the model. Own everything else. 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 English · 简体中文 
 

CoWork OS is a free, open-source AI agent desktop app for macOS and Windows that does real work for you: files, documents, the browser, your inbox and scheduled jobs. It is a local-first alternative to Claude Cowork and OpenClaw: bring your own API key for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter and other providers, or run local models through Ollama, and message it from WhatsApp, Telegram or Slack. You watch every step as it happens, and with the default Ask for approval profile the agent works freely inside your workspace but stops and asks before anything that leaves it: sending, network access, credentials, exports, or files outside the workspace. Use the model you choose; your workspace, memory, skills and history stay on your machine. Model providers may charge for usage and receive the data needed for the tasks you run. What you own

 
 
 

 MIT licensed · runs on your machine · 17,000+ automated tests · independent security assessment · contributions welcome 

 What you can do with it

- Turn a folder of files into finished work. "Make a spreadsheet of these invoices with a total per vendor" — the spreadsheet opens beside the chat, editable, and you can ask for changes in place.
- Get through your inbox without losing control. It triages, summarizes and drafts replies; nothing is sent until you approve it.
- Research in a browser you can watch. The agent browses in a visible window you can take over at any time, and hands back a report with its sources.
- Put a bot on a schedule. A bot with its own memory posts a morning summary to Telegram, Slack or Discord, and asks you before it acts outside its scope.
- Make 3D models and game assets. "Make a low-poly treasure chest for my Godot game" — Meshy builds it, the approval card names the credit cost first, and the model appears in the chat as a 3D view you can spin, animate and download. 3D Models with Meshy
- Work on code with every command shown. Real terminal tabs, diffs and test runs in the timeline, and approvals for anything risky.
- Keep it all local if you want. Run on Ollama or LM Studio on your own machine, or sign in with OpenRouter and use free models with no API key to copy.

 Every risky step waits for your answer

 --- --- 
 See every step, approve the risky ones The timeline shows each file read, command and edit as it happens. Access profiles (Ask for approval, Approve for me, Full access, Custom) decide what waits for you, and hard limits hold even if you approve. Access profiles 
 Get finished files, not just answers Documents, spreadsheets, decks, web pages and PDFs open beside the agent, editable, and you can ask for changes without starting over. Everything Workbench 
 An inbox that drafts, you send Local-first triage, search across your mail, and reply drafts; sending always waits for you. Inbox Agent 
 A browser you can watch and take over Real tabs that stay loaded, downloads and history, and logins filled only on the exact site after you confirm. Browser Workbench 
 Bots that work while you don't Bots with their own memory, model and schedule, reachable on Telegram, Slack, Discord, WhatsApp and more. Bots · Channels 
 Memory you can open and edit What CoWork knows about you is plain markdown in a local git folder: read it, change it, sync it or delete it. Memory 
 Any model you choose, switch any time OpenRouter sign-in with free models, ChatGPT sign-in, local Ollama or LM Studio, or API keys for Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Groq and more, per conversation. Models & Access 

 Why CoWork OS?

 If you use… You might choose CoWork OS when you want… 
 --- --- 
 A terminal agent (Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Claude Code) The same kind of agent in a desktop app, with approvals you can see, files that open beside the chat, and memory you can read. CoWork can import a Hermes or OpenClaw setup. 
 A hosted desktop assistant (ChatGPT, Claude Cowork) An open-source app where you pick the model, run local models, and keep your workspace, memory and history on your machine. 
 A coding agent (Cursor, Codex) One workspace for code and everything around it: documents, inbox, browser, bots and schedules. 

These are fit notes, not rankings; see Compare CoWork OS for each product's strengths and the evidence behind each page.

Linux servers: use the packaged headless server. Re-run the same command to update.

 
 Trouble installing? Use the DMG or EXE instead 

Download the installer from GitHub Releases. Releases are not notarized by Apple or code signed for Windows, so a browser download needs one extra step the first time:

- macOS DMG: drag CoWork OS into Applications and open it. When macOS says it was not opened, click Done , then go to System Settings Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway . Step-by-step screenshots: macOS Installation.
- Windows EXE: when SmartScreen says Windows protected your PC , click More info Run anyway . Checksums and antivirus notes: Windows Installation.
- macOS 12 Monterey: 0.5.51 is the last compatible release: npm install -g cowork-os@0.5.51 .

 

 Getting started

1. Open CoWork OS. On macOS the first start may ask for the cowork-os Safe Storage keychain item; click Always Allow .
2. Pick a model. Choose Continue with OpenRouter for free models with no API key to copy (from 0.5.61), sign in with ChatGPT, use a detected local Ollama model, or paste an API key. Free options are marked, and you can switch models any time.

install.title: Install
install.html:
macOS (Apple Silicon, macOS 13 or later). No Gatekeeper dialog:

curl -fsSL https://coworkosapp.com/install.sh | bash

Windows (64-bit), in PowerShell. No SmartScreen prompt:

irm https://coworkosapp.com/install.ps1 | iex

Any platform with Node.js 24, including Intel Macs. Installs the desktop app and the cowork CLI:

npm install -g cowork-os

Linux servers: use the packaged headless server. Re-run the same command to update.

Trouble installing? Use the DMG or EXE instead

Download the installer from GitHub Releases. Releases are not notarized by Apple or code signed for Windows, so a browser download needs one extra step the first time:

  • macOS DMG: drag CoWork OS into Applications and open it. When macOS says it was not opened, click Done, then go to System Settings > Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway. Step-by-step screenshots: macOS Installation.
  • Windows EXE: when SmartScreen says Windows protected your PC, click More info > Run anyway. Checksums and antivirus notes: Windows Installation.
  • macOS 12 Monterey: 0.5.51 is the last compatible release: npm install -g cowork-os@0.5.51.
